name: q061
question:
How are pulsars formed?
Pulsars are rotating neutron stars that produce pulses of radio waves, X-rays, and gamma rays. They are formed when a massive star runs out of fuel and collapses in on itself. The remnants are neutron stars with magnetic fields that range in strength from 100 million times to 1 quadrillion (a million billion) times that of Earth’s. The correct mix of spin frequency and magnetic field strength is needed for a neutron star to be a pulsar. A pulsar’s radiation bursts typically repeat in a time range anywhere from milliseconds to seconds. It is believed that millisecond pulsars may have formed by consuming fuel from another companion object, thus earning the moniker “black widow pulsars.”
title: How are pulsars formed?
